name: Hydroxypropyl distarch phosphate
what_it_is: Ordinary starch, changed slightly so that it holds up to heat, acid and freezing.
why_its_added: Thickens sauces and fillings and keeps them stable after cooking or freezing.

india.note: Maximum level depends on the food. Examples below.

eu.note: EFSA has assessed the safety of this additive, but we have no public record of its current authorisation in the EU.

eu_safety_opinion.title: Re‐evaluation of oxidised starch (E 1404), monostarch phosphate (E 1410), distarch phosphate (E 1412), phosphated distarch phosphate (E 1413), acetylated distarch phosphate (E 1414), acetylated starch (E 1420), acetylated distarch adipate (E 1422), hydroxypropyl starch (E 1440), hydroxypropyl distarch phosphate (E 1442), starch sodium octenyl succinate (E 1450), acetylated oxidised starch (E 1451) and starch aluminium octenyl succinate (E 1452) as food additives

safe_daily_limit.no_number_means: EFSA has not set a number for this one. That can mean it is considered safe enough not to need a limit, or that the evidence was not sufficient to set one. The opinion itself says which.

means: No single-serving limit has been found for this substance. That is not the same as there being no risk from one large serving - it means nobody has published a number.

people_reports.rule: Reports are shown as reports. We count them. We never turn them into a health claim, and we never let them change the sourced facts above.

india_limits.food_category: Sterilized and UHT creams, whipping and whipped creams, and reduced fat creams (plain)
Dried whey and whey products, excluding whey cheeses
Frozen battered fish, fish fillets and fish products, including molluscs, crustaceans, and echinoderms Trisodium
Coffee, coffee /coffee substitutes, tea, herbal infusions, and other hot cereal and grain beverages, excluding cocoa
